name: Madras Christian College
summary: Madras Christian College began on 3 April 1837 as the General Assembly School, founded by Rev. John Anderson of the Church of Scotland, and moved to its Tambaram campus — a 390-acre stretch of the Selaiyur forest — in 1937. It became one of the earliest autonomous colleges in 1978 and is affiliated to the University of Madras. Undergraduate courses run in an aided stream and a self-financed stream; admission is on Class XII marks.

admission.eligibility: A pass in the Tamil Nadu Higher Secondary or an equivalent examination; Plus Two marks are required to apply. Boards other than the Tamil Nadu State Board, CBSE (AISSCE) and CISCE need an eligibility certificate from the University of Madras, as do private-study and open-school candidates.
admission.reservation: Selection lists are drawn up by community category (e.g. OC).

process.detail: The 2026–27 portal opened on 23 February 2026; admissions begin after the Tamil Nadu Class XII results.
Selection lists are published by programme, ranked on Class XII percentage within each community category.
Admitted students pay the course fee to confirm the seat.
Hall (hostel) places are applied for separately to the Dean of Students' Affairs after paying course fees.
